subject: Contract redline: inference telemetry & data isolation exception request
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex@ingestai.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: ingestai-legal@ingestai.com
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: IngestAI redline: runtime telemetry and data isolation

Hi Grace,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — team was impressed by the latency profile. Legal ran a pass on the DPA and returned a short set of redlines. The core ask they pushed back on is telemetry: they want to receive more granular telemetry for debugging (partial prompt hash, anonymized IP ranges, and request-level latency with model variant identifiers) and to allow a 30-day retention window for that telemetry in our analytics subsystem.

They understand this is outside the standard telemetry retention and are asking for an exception in our DPA Exhibit for this account only (pilot phase). They also requested confirmation of which subprocessors would touch telemetry (specifically any third-party analytics or observability vendors).

Attached is a PDF with inline redlines (ingestai_dpa_redlines_v3.pdf). Can you route to Product and Security for an internal feasibility and risk assessment? We need a response to procurement by EOB Monday.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Morgan
Head of Engineering, IngestAI

Attachments: ingestai_dpa_redlines_v3.pdf (pdf, 120KB)
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 10:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: IngestAI redline: runtime telemetry and data isolation

Team — forwarding IngestAI's redlines. Procurement wants a definitive yes/no + mitigation by Monday COB.

Quick summary of asks from legal:
- Allow runtime telemetry retention up to 30 days for pilot (current default 7 days)
- Include partial prompt hash and model-variant id in telemetry that may be stored
- Provide list of subprocessors that will see telemetry (analytics, SSO, observability)

Product: can we support 30d retention for telemetry only on a per-account flag? How much operational effort to keep KV/cache traces out and persist metadata?
Security: what are the minimum controls (encryption at rest, access controls, redaction) to satisfy you for sign-off?

Attaching their redline and a quick impact sheet (prod-impact-matrix.xlsx). Please reply-all with explicit signoff or escalations.

— Grace
Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference
From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 13:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: IngestAI redline: runtime telemetry and data isolation

Thanks Grace,

High-level security stance: we can consider a scoped exception for telemetry retention if the following constraints are met and documented in an exception ticket:
1) Telemetry must be pseudonymized at ingest — store only a salted hash for prompt fragments; no plaintext prompts or prompt completions may be persisted.
2) IP addresses must be reduced to /24 (IPv4) or /64 (IPv6) and logged only as ranges.
3) Data at rest must use customer-specific KMS keys (BYOK where available) or a per-account envelope key managed by Redwood with strict access controls for product/ops.
4) Access reviews: only named SREs and the customer's audit users can access telemetry; access logs must be retained for the same 30-day window and are subject to audit.
5) Subprocessor disclosure: list all telemetry processors and confirm no analytics vendor will receive raw prompt content.

Open questions for Product (Marcus):
- Can we flip a per-account telemetry retention flag and enforce pseudonymization at ingest before the analytics pipeline?
- What's the expected overhead (storage/cost) for 30d vs 7d at IngestAI pilot scale (~200M tokens/month)?

If Product can commit to pseudonymization + per-account KMS, Security can provisionally approve the exception pending a short runbook and audit checklist.

- Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: marcus_lin@redwood.com
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 04 Jun 2028 08:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: IngestAI redline: runtime telemetry and data isolation

Folks — did a quick feasibility & impact pass with Infra. Summary:
- Technical approach: implement a per-account telemetry retention policy and a pseudonymization layer at the telemetry inbound stage. We'll hash prompt fragments with a salted HMAC (salt scoped to account) and persist only the HMAC + length bucket (so we can debug short vs long requests). No plaintext prompt storage.
- IPs: can truncate to /24 and store as such.
- KMS: we can wire a per-account envelope key and rotate monthly; BYOK would require legal + infra onboarding and will add ~2 weeks to timeline.
- Cost: approximate increase in analytics storage + retrieval estimated at +18% for 30d vs 7d at the projected pilot volume. We captured numbers in prod-impact-matrix.xlsx.
- Ops: requires a short runbook for escalation and an RBAC change to grant telemetry access to a named SRE group + IngestAI's audit user.

Timeline: we can have a guarded pilot pipeline ready in ~10 business days if Security signs off on the pseudonymization specifics and KMS approach. BYOK would add time.

If Security is comfortable with the HMAC approach and truncated IP storage, Product is OK to support the contractual carveout limited to the pilot and documented in an internal exception ticket. Need Security's explicit written signoff to communicate to Procurement.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Product Manager, Runtime | Redwood Inference
From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com, ingestai-legal@ingestai.com
Date: Mon, 04 Jun 2028 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Contract redline: inference telemetry & data isolation exception request

Thanks all — quick summary for procurement & customer:
- Product (Marcus) confirms per-account retention flag + pseudonymization (HMAC of prompt fragments) and IP truncation to /24 are implementable. Estimated cost delta ~+18% for storage.
- Security (Olga) has provisionally approved the exception contingent on: encrypted-at-rest with per-account envelope key, named SRE access controls, and a runbook + audit checklist to be uploaded to the exception ticket.
- BYOK: optional but will add ~2 weeks; will offer as follow-up if customer wants full key control.

Next steps:
1) Olivia (Security) to upload the short security runbook and sign-off note to INF-1293 by EOD Wed.
2) Product to open a pilot change request and target pipeline rollout in ~10 business days.
3) I'll reply to IngestAI (below) with the conditional acceptance and the caveat that final legal language will reference the internal exception ticket and the runbook.

IngestAI legal — Grace to IngestAI: we can accept the telemetry retention carveout for the pilot under the controls above. Please confirm you accept the per-account pseudonymization, IP truncation, and that you will not request raw prompt exports from Redwood. Once we have Security's short runbook uploaded, we'll share the final edited Exhibit.

— Grace
Grace O'Connor
Director, Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference
